findings.anchor: if (any(unicodedata.category(c) in ("No", "Cf", "Cn") or any(a <= ord(c) <= b for a, b in oa) for c in h)
findings.description: The new Unicode gate in gh_anchor refuses categories No, Cf and Cn but admits Cc and Zl/Zp. san1 (the only sanitizer the title passes through) strips C0 control bytes and flattens \t \n \r, but it works on bytes under LC_ALL=C and never sees Unicode line terminators or C1 controls: NEL U+0085 (Cc), LINE SEPARATOR U+2028 (Zl), PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR U+2029 (Zp) and U+0080–U+009F (Cc) all survive into the heading line written by op_new and into the log/die messages that echo the title. Because `word()` returns false for these, the anchor is unaffected and the writer's own grep/awk/`\n`-based checks (duplicate check, next_kf_id, verify_and_swap's drop guard) see one physical line, so the write succeeds. Any consumer that splits on Unicode line boundaries (Python str.splitlines(), Java BufferedReader, many editors) sees `## KF-003: foo<U+2028>## KF-999: fake` as two headings, so a caller can smuggle a phantom `## KF-NNN:` heading or `| [KF-NNN](#…) |` Index row into such a reader while the shell-side integrity checks stay green. C1 controls (e.g. U+009B CSI, U+009D OSC) additionally reach the operator's terminal via `log`/`die` on xterm-class terminals that honour UTF-8-encoded C1.
findings.failure_mode: The single-line / control-free invariant that san1 is meant to enforce is ASCII-only; the new Unicode category filter was the natural place to close that gap and does not. A crafted --title injects extra logical lines for Unicode-aware readers of known-failures.md and can carry terminal control sequences into stderr output.
findings.suggested_fix: In the python3 gate, also exit 4 (or strip) for any c with unicodedata.category(c) in ("Cc", "Zl", "Zp") — this covers U+0085 and U+0080–U+009F as well as U+2028/U+2029 — and apply the same check to the ASCII/byte path by routing every non-ASCII title through python3 before the C1 bytes can be echoed. Alternatively extend san1 to delete the UTF-8 byte sequences \xC2[\x80-\x9F], \xE2\x80\xA8 and \xE2\x80\xA9.

findings.anchor:
printf '
### Reading guide

%s
' "$(san1 "${A[reading-guide]-TODO: what a future agent should do on this symptom.}")"
findings.description: The diff adds gh_title_renders_raw so a --title cannot carry Markdown that changes how the heading renders (`<!` and `<[A-Za-z/!?]` are refused, among others), and adds a ledger lint whose stated invariant is that every Index link resolves to a rendered heading. But the two values op_new and op_notes_header write as FREE-STANDING lines — --reading-guide and --note — get only san1, which trims leading whitespace and so places the value at column 0. A value of ``` or ~~~ opens a fenced block, and a value of <!-- opens a CommonMark type-2 HTML block that ends only at a later line containing -->. Since a new entry is appended at the end of the file, every entry written afterwards sits inside that block: on GitHub its `## KF-NNN:` heading is not a heading, its anchor does not exist, and the Evidence rows are invisible. The new lint skips fenced blocks (so a ``` reading guide would at least fail CI) but does not model HTML blocks, so the <!-- variant passes the lint, passes verify_and_swap (grep still sees the headings) and passes kf-auto-link.py-style `^##\s+KF-` readers, while hiding the ledger from human readers on GitHub — the exact anti-tamper property the file header says this helper exists to protect.
findings.failure_mode: A single kf-write new --reading-guide '<!--' (or notes-header --note '<!--') call by the automation that is supposed to be constrained by this helper renders all later known-failures entries invisible on GitHub without tripping the writer's guards or the new link lint.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate free-standing values the way titles are now gated: refuse (or prefix with inline text so they are never at column 0) any --reading-guide/--note value matching a CommonMark block starter at line start — ^ {0,3}(```|~~~|<!--|<\?|<![A-Z]|<[A-Za-z]|#{1,6}( |$)|[-*+] |[0-9]{1,9}[.)] |>|\||[-*_]{3,}\s*$). Teach _kf_link_lint to skip HTML blocks (type 1 and 2 at minimum: lines from `<!--` to a line containing `-->`, and `<pre|<script|<style|<textarea` to their closing tag) exactly as it skips fences, so the shipped-ledger test detects a hidden tail.
